chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from al-Abbas, from Safwan, who said:

The Marzuban asked him about a man who commits fornication with a woman while she is the daughter (unmarried) of another people, then he buys her daughter; is it permissible for him to marry her? He said, 'That which is haram does not make halal haram.' And [asked about] a man who commits fornication with a woman in a forbidden manner; is he permitted to marry her daughter? He said, 'That which is haram does not make halal haram.'

The meaning in this report is what we have previously stated, that if the fornication is before consummation (sexual intercourse), then as for with consummation, it is not permissible according to what we have previously stated, and that which clarifies it further is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْمَرْزُبَانُ: Marzuban (a Persian governor or official title)
key_terms.لاَ يُحَرِّمُ الْحَرَامُ الْحَلاَلَ: That which is haram does not make halal haram

ai.seo_question: Does fornication with a woman prohibit marrying her daughter in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the principle of 'la yuharrimu al-haramu al-halala' (forbidden acts do not render permissible what was previously lawful) regarding marriage eligibility. Shia scholars distinguish between non-consummated fornication, which does not prohibit marrying the daughter, and consummated fornication, which does, based on the precedent established in this narration.
